quest.title: A Robust Theoretical Discussion
quest.description: Near the Fountain of Lucine, you and Paimon seem to hear someone arguing...

talks.objective: Look for the source of the arguing

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: Alright, here comes our main character! Get the cameras rolling!

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: ...Huh! No, no, that's not right! A business partnership should be like a film script. It needs a proper structure, with a beginning, middle, and end!

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: Typically, the first thing you do when you approach a superstar for a partnership is offer them your business card. You then follow that up with a grand introduction to properly position yourself, then pitch them your vision for the partnership.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: You only start to talk about the specifics of the partnership once they show a certain degree of interest. The way you went about talking about your Flash Cuts idea? That was way too much, too soon!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: To be frank, Miss Melies, that theory of yours might hold a little more water if your debut film, "Experimental Studio," hadn't been such a flop.

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: #Besides, you tried to approach {NICKNAME} back at Film Fantasyland, didn't you? But if I'm right, you didn't seem to have left much of an impression on {M#him}{F#her} at all.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: ...Everything you've said is nothing more than the fanciful thinking of a child! The adult world is far more complicated. It's not as simple as you think!

dialogues.speaker: Petit Lumiere
dialogues.text: Oh dear. How terribly superficial of you to use someone's age to debunk their argument, Miss Melies. Your behavior right now only proves my point.

dialogues.speaker: Melies
dialogues.text: What in the world are you saying? Hah! You pretentious little brat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Hold on, hold on, there's no need to raise your voice! Can't we just sit down and talk this out calmly?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: #Um... Did {NICKNAME} and Paimon really just come to us? I can't believe that worked...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Look, Miss Melies. It's like what I said — people care more about the eye-catching parts than a long-drawn-out setup.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: We're talking about folks so famous, you might stand in line for three days and three nights and still not get to talk to them. But now, they've approached us simply because they saw us arguing.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: And now, this is the part we pitch our proposed partnership...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Ahem. You came at just the right time, you two. What do you think about our Flash Cuts pilot? It's a real attention-grabber, don't you think?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What "Cut" now? Weren't you two...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: What, having a fight? Haha, no, not at all. An adult as dignified as her wouldn't get worked up over the words of a mere "brat" now, would she?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Pfft. That's true. Especially when I'm dealing with precocious brats who act like they're all grown-up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That doesn't sound like "not a fight" at all...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Anyway, don't you think that walking right into a high-tension scene like that would make anyone want to see the rest?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Anyone" would try to stop the argument, you mean.

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: But what if you'd known back there that we were shooting a short film?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, you do have a point... If it's something that interests Paimon from the get-go, Paimon would definitely want to keep watching...

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: And that's the USP for Flash Cuts — the viewer gets to see the most gripping, most emotionally charged content in the shortest time possible!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Not only that, unlike regular short films, Flash Cuts are designed for quick viewing — between tasks or while you're on the move. You can easily watch one while taking a break on your travels!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: And you don't have to be a professional director or cameraman to make a Flash Cut. Anyone can create or watch a Flash Cut anytime, anywhere.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Content-wise, you aren't restricted to storytelling either — your Flash Cut can be about anything from a dance to just some beautiful scenery. Doesn't a format like that sound enticing to you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, it sure does. Now Paimon wants to shoot a Flash Cut herself too...

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: But of course, we'll need some star power to guarantee we get the eyeballs we need! And that means we need someone whose name is known in every corner of Teyvat!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: That's right — I'm talking about you two!!!

choices.text: You do know that stars command hefty appearance fees, right...?

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Oh, please rest assured that Mr. Petit Lumiere and I have, after our time at Film Fantasyland, raised enough money. You'll certainly get your appearance fee!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: #Besides, think about how you might become known as the {M#Father}{F#Mother} of Flash Cuts once we make it big!

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Not only that, Flash Cuts has truly pushed the boundaries of filmic language. With your experience behind the lens, you'll be able to narrate purely through visuals, without needing any dialogue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #This all sounds really fun! Shall we give it a try, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Petit Lumiere
response.text: Excellent! We'll start shooting as soon as the two of you are ready. I've already selected the camera positions.

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: I also have the Film Kamera, props, and post-production lined up as well. All you need to do is use them as you please!

response.speaker: Melies
response.text: Then let's get to it!

choices.text: So we'll get paid? Sure, let's give it a shot then!
That is, if this is a commission at all.
I'm sure whatever it is, we can work it out...
